Canagliflozin Inhibits Electrogenic Na+ Transport in Mouse Cortical Collecting Duct Cells. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) exhibit cardiorenal protective effects that likely involve mechanisms aside from SGLT2 inhibition. Still, many details surrounding these clinically important pleiotropic effects remain unclear. An SGLT2 inhibitor, canagliflozin, reduces blood glucose level in the renal capillaries and protects the capillary network in the diabetic rats. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors consistently demonstrate renal protection against progressive kidney disease. We hypothesised that SGLT2 inhibition reduces blood glucose levels in peri-proximal tubular capillaries by limiting reabsorption from the tubular filtrate, thereby safeguarding the renal microvasculature from hyperglycaemic stress.
